==Problem==
Greta Grasshopper sits on a long line of lily pads in a pond. From any lily pad, Greta can jump <imath>5</imath> pads to the right or <imath>3</imath> pads to the left. What is the fewest number of jumps Greta must make to reach the lily pad located <imath>2023</imath> pads to the right of her starting position?

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 405 \qquad \textbf{(B) } 407 \qquad \textbf{(C) } 409 \qquad \textbf{(D) } 411 \qquad \textbf{(E) } 413</imath>

==Solution 1==
We have <imath>2</imath> directions going <imath>5</imath> right or <imath>3</imath> left. We can assign a variable to each of these directions. We can call going right <imath>1</imath> direction <imath>\text{X}</imath> and we can call going <imath>1</imath> left <imath>\text{Y}</imath>. We can build an equation of <imath>5\text{X}-3\text{Y}=2023</imath>, where we have to limit the number of moves we do. We can do this by making more of our moves the <imath>5</imath> move turn than the <imath>3</imath> move turn. The first obvious step is to go some amount of moves in the right direction then subtract off in the left direction to land on <imath>2023</imath>. The least amount of <imath>3</imath>’s added to <imath>2023</imath> to make a multiple of <imath>5</imath> is <imath>4</imath> as <imath>2023 + 4(3) = 2035</imath>. So now, we have solved the problem as we just go <imath>\frac{2035}{5} = 407</imath> hops right, and just do 4 more hops left. Yielding <imath>407 + 4 = \boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 411}</imath> as our answer.

~apex304, SohumUttamchandani, wuwang2002, TaeKim, Cxrupptedpat

==Solution 2==
Notice that <imath>2023 \equiv 3\pmod{5}</imath>, and jumping to the left increases the value of Greta's position <imath>\pmod{5}</imath> by <imath>2</imath>. Therefore, the number of jumps to the left must be <imath>4 \pmod{5}</imath>. As the number of jumps to the left increases, so does the number of jumps to the right, we must minimize both, which occurs when we jump <imath>4</imath> to the left and <imath>407</imath> to the right. The answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 411}</imath>.

~TRALALA

==Solution 3==

<imath>5y - 2023</imath> must be divisible by 3. The smallest value of <imath>y</imath> that will achieve this is <imath>407</imath>, which lands it at <imath>2035</imath>. After that, it takes <imath>4</imath> jumps back, making a total of <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 411}</imath>.

~e___

==Solution 3.1==
Here is Solution 3 but worded differently:
We can to go back <imath>3x</imath> steps from <imath>5y</imath> steps we took past <imath>2023</imath>. The other way to say this is we go <imath>3x</imath> steps from <imath>2023</imath> to get to <imath>5y</imath>. What is the least value of <imath>3x</imath>? We need <imath>2023+3x</imath> to end in a <imath>5</imath> or <imath>0</imath>. The least value for <imath>3x</imath>, which makes <imath>2023+3x=2035</imath>, is <imath>4</imath>. <imath>\frac{2035}{5}=407</imath>. Therefore, <imath>407+4=</imath> <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 411}</imath>.

==Solution 4 (Easy to understand and simple)==
Greta needs to jump <imath>2023</imath> steps to the right. Since we want (a multiple of <imath>5</imath>)- (a multiple of <imath>3</imath>) that ends in a <imath>3</imath>. The smallest this can be is <imath>15</imath> - <imath>12</imath> = <imath>3</imath>. 

We can apply this to the problem; the closest number that ends in <imath>15</imath> from <imath>2023</imath> is <imath>2015</imath>. (Note that <imath>2015</imath> is <imath>403</imath> jumps (every <imath>5</imath> jumps to the right is one lily pad, we will use this later.) 

From this, we know that to get to <imath>2003</imath> steps, Greta would have to jump <imath>12</imath> pads to the left, which would take <imath>4</imath> jumps from the lily pad (every <imath>3</imath> jumps to the left is one lily pad). 

Lastly, to get to <imath>2023</imath>, it would take <imath>20</imath> pads to the right, which would be <imath>4</imath> jumps from the lily pads as well.

In total, this is <imath>403</imath> + <imath>4</imath> + <imath>4</imath> = <imath>411</imath> , or <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 411}</imath>.

~OddPeppyBoots
